evidence: This describes a property of the V1 receptive field inference problem.

claim: The posterior distribution for the V1 receptive field has multiple peaks ('modes').
source: As a result, the posterior distribution has multiple peaks ('modes').
evidence: This describes a property of the posterior distribution for the V1 problem.

claim: The authors fed the CNN's output into a mixture density network (MDN) to deal with the multiple peaks in the posterior.
source: To deal with the multiple peaks in the posterior, we fed the CNN's output into a mixture density network (MDN) (Bishop, 1994), which can learn to assign probability distributions with multiple peaks as a function of its inputs (details in Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the network architecture used with citation.

claim: For the V1 receptive field problem with high-dimensional summary features, an SMC-ABC algorithm with the same simulation-budget failed to identify the correct receptive fields.
source: For this challenging estimation problem with high-dimensional summary features, an SMC-ABC algorithm with the same simulation-budget failed to identify the correct receptive fields (Figure 2g) and posterior distributions (Appendix 1—figure 5).
evidence: This is a result comparing SNPE to SMC-ABC.

claim: The authors applied SNPE to electrophysiological data from a V1 cell, identifying a sine-shaped Gabor receptive field consistent with the original spike-triggered average.
source: We also applied this approach to electrophysiological data from a V1 cell (Dyballa et al., 2018), identifying a sine-shaped Gabor receptive field consistent with the original spike-triggered average (Figure 2i; posterior distribution in Appendix 1—figure 6).
evidence: This is a result from applying SNPE to real data with citation.

claim: The authors considered a flexible model of ion channels (Destexhe and Huguenard, 2000), referred to as the Omnimodel.
source: We considered a flexible model of ion channels (Destexhe and Huguenard, 2000), which we here refer to as the Omnimodel.
evidence: This describes the model used for ion channel inference with citation.

claim: The Omnimodel uses eight parameters to describe how the dynamics of currents through non-inactivating potassium channels depend on membrane voltage.
source: This model uses eight parameters to describe how the dynamics of currents through non-inactivating potassium channels depend on membrane voltage (Figure 3a).
evidence: This describes the Omnimodel.

claim: For various choices of its parameters θ, the Omnimodel can capture 350 specific models in publications describing non-inactivating potassium channels, cataloged in the IonChannelGenealogy (ICG) database.
source: For various choices of its parameters 𝜽, it can capture 350 specific models in publications describing this channel type, cataloged in the IonChannelGenealogy (ICG) database (Podlaski et al., 2017).
evidence: This describes the capability of the Omnimodel with citation.

claim: The authors aimed to identify ion channel parameters θ for each ICG model, based on 11 features of the model's response to a sequence of five noisy voltage clamp protocols, resulting in a total of 55 different characteristic features per model.
source: We aimed to identify these ion channel parameters 𝜽 for each ICG model, based on 11 features of the model's response to a sequence of five noisy voltage clamp protocols, resulting in a total of 55 different characteristic features per model (Figure 3b, see Materials and methods for details).
evidence: This describes the inference task for ion channels.

claim: The ability to rapidly infer different parameters for many separate experiments is advantageous for ion channel models.
source: Because this model's output is a typical format for functional characterization of ion channels both in simulations (Podlaski et al., 2017) and in high-throughput electrophysiological experiments (Dunlop et al., 2008; Suk et al., 2019; Ranjan et al., 2019), the ability to rapidly infer different parameters for many separate experiments is advantageous.
evidence: This explains the motivation for amortized inference with citations.

claim: Existing fitting approaches based on numerical optimization must repeat all computations anew for a new experiment or data point.
source: Existing fitting approaches based on numerical optimization (Destexhe and Huguenard, 2000; Ranjan et al., 2019) must repeat all computations anew for a new experiment or data point (Figure 3c).
evidence: This describes a limitation of existing approaches with citations.

claim: For SNPE the only heavy computational tasks are carrying out simulations to generate training data, and training the neural network.
source: However, for SNPE the only heavy computational tasks are carrying out simulations to generate training data, and training the neural network.
evidence: This describes the computational requirements of SNPE.

claim: By training a network once using a large number of simulations, SNPE can subsequently carry out rapid 'amortized' parameter inference on new data using a single pass through the network.
source: We therefore reasoned that by training a network once using a large number of simulations, we could subsequently carry out rapid 'amortized' parameter inference on new data using a single pass through the network (Figure 3d; Speiser et al., 2017; Webb et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes the amortized inference capability of SNPE with citations.

claim: The authors used SNPE to train a neural network to infer the posterior from any data x for the Omnimodel.
source: To test this idea, we used SNPE to train a neural network to infer the posterior from any data 𝐱.
evidence: This describes the application of SNPE to the Omnimodel.

claim: The authors carried out 1 million Omnimodel simulations to generate training data.
source: To generate training data, we carried out 1 million Omnimodel simulations, with parameters randomly chosen across ranges large enough to capture the models in the ICG database (Podlaski et al., 2017).
evidence: This describes the training data generation with citation.

claim: SNPE was run using a single round for the Omnimodel, learning to perform inference for all data from the prior.
source: SNPE was run using a single round, that is, it learned to perform inference for all data from the prior (rather than a specific observed datum).
evidence: This describes the training procedure for the Omnimodel.

claim: Generating 1 million Omnimodel simulations took around 1000 CPU-hours and training the network 150 CPU-hours.
source: Generating these simulations took around 1000 CPU-hours and training the network 150 CPU-hours, but afterwards a full posterior distribution could be inferred for new data in less than 10 ms.
evidence: This provides computational cost information.

claim: After training, a full posterior distribution could be inferred for new data in less than 10 ms for the Omnimodel.
source: Generating these simulations took around 1000 CPU-hours and training the network 150 CPU-hours, but afterwards a full posterior distribution could be inferred for new data in less than 10 ms.
evidence: This demonstrates the speed of amortized inference.

claim: The authors evaluated SNPE's performance on all 350 non-inactivating potassium channel models in ICG.
source: Taking advantage of SNPE's capability for rapid amortized inference, we further evaluated its performance on all 350 non-inactivating potassium channel models in ICG.
evidence: This describes an evaluation of SNPE.

claim: For each ICG model, the authors carried out a simulation to generate initial data, used SNPE to calculate the posterior, and then generated a new simulation using parameters sampled from the posterior.
source: In each case, we carried out a simulation to generate initial data from the original ICG model, used SNPE to calculate the posterior given the Omnimodel, and then generated a new simulation 𝐱 using parameters sampled from the posterior (Figure 3f).
evidence: This describes the evaluation procedure.

claim: SNPE resulted in high correlation between the original ICG model response and the Omnimodel response (>0.98 for more than 90% of models).
source: This resulted in high correlation between the original ICG model response and the Omnimodel response, in every case (>0.98 for more than 90% of models, see Appendix 1—figure 7).
evidence: This is a result from the evaluation.

claim: SNPE was not able to capture all traces perfectly, as it failed to capture the shape of the onset of one model in Figure 3g.
source: However, this approach was not able to capture all traces perfectly, as for example it failed to capture the shape of the onset of the bottom right model in Figure 3g.
evidence: This describes a limitation observed in the results.

claim: The failure to capture one trace is not a failure of SNPE, but rather a limitation of the Omnimodel.
source: Additional analysis of this example revealed that this example is not a failure of SNPE, but rather a limitation of the Omnimodel: in particular, directly fitting the steady-state activation and time-constant curves on this specific example yielded no further quantitative or qualitative improvement, suggesting that the limitation is in the model, not the fit.
evidence: This is an inference from additional analysis.

claim: SNPE can be used to reveal limitations of candidate models and aid the development of more verisimilar mechanistic models.
source: Thus, SNPE can be used to reveal limitations of candidate models and aid the development of more verisimilar mechanistic models.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the results.

claim: Calculating the posterior for all 350 ICG models took only a few seconds, and was fully automated.
source: Calculating the posterior for all 350 ICG models took only a few seconds, and was fully automated, that is, did not require user interactions.
evidence: This demonstrates the efficiency of amortized inference.

claim: SNPE allows fast and accurate identification of biophysical model parameters on new data.
source: These results show how SNPE allows fast and accurate identification of biophysical model parameters on new data, and how SNPE can be deployed for applications requiring rapid automated inference, such as high-throughput screening-assays, closed-loop paradigms (e.g. for adaptive experimental manipulations or stimulus-selection [Kleinegesse and Gutmann, 2019]), or interactive software tools.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the ion channel results with citation.

claim: SNPE can be deployed for applications requiring rapid automated inference, such as high-throughput screening-assays, closed-loop paradigms, or interactive software tools.
source: These results show how SNPE allows fast and accurate identification of biophysical model parameters on new data, and how SNPE can be deployed for applications requiring rapid automated inference, such as high-throughput screening-assays, closed-loop paradigms (e.g. for adaptive experimental manipulations or stimulus-selection [Kleinegesse and Gutmann, 2019]), or interactive software tools.
evidence: This describes potential applications of SNPE with citation.

claim: The Hodgkin–Huxley (HH) model of action potential generation through ion channel dynamics is a highly influential mechanistic model in neuroscience.
source: The Hodgkin–Huxley (HH) model (Hodgkin and Huxley, 1952) of action potential generation through ion channel dynamics is a highly influential mechanistic model in neuroscience.
evidence: This describes the importance of the HH model with citation.

claim: A number of algorithms have been proposed for fitting HH models to electrophysiological data.
source: A number of algorithms have been proposed for fitting HH models to electrophysiological data (Prinz et al., 2003; Huys et al., 2006; Pospischil et al., 2008; Rossant et al., 2011; Meliza et al., 2014; Van Geit et al., 2016; Ben-Shalom et al., 2019), but (with the exception of Daly et al., 2015) these approaches do not attempt to estimate the full posterior.
evidence: This describes prior work on HH model fitting with citations.

claim: With the exception of Daly et al., 2015, previous approaches for fitting HH models do not attempt to estimate the full posterior.
source: A number of algorithms have been proposed for fitting HH models to electrophysiological data (Prinz et al., 2003; Huys et al., 2006; Pospischil et al., 2008; Rossant et al., 2011; Meliza et al., 2014; Van Geit et al., 2016; Ben-Shalom et al., 2019), but (with the exception of Daly et al., 2015) these approaches do not attempt to estimate the full posterior.
evidence: This describes a limitation of prior work with citations.

claim: Previous approaches for HH models concentrated on reproducing specified features (e.g. the number of spikes).
source: As previous approaches for HH models concentrated on reproducing specified features (e.g. the number of spikes, [Pospischil et al., 2008]), we also sought to determine how various features provide different constraints.
evidence: This describes prior work with citation.

claim: The authors considered the problem of inferring eight biophysical parameters in a HH single-compartment model.
source: We considered the problem of inferring eight biophysical parameters in a HH single-compartment model, describing voltage-dependent sodium and potassium conductances and other intrinsic membrane properties, including neural noise, making the model stochastic by nature (Figure 4a, left).
evidence: This describes the inference problem for the HH model.

claim: The HH model includes neural noise, making the model stochastic by nature.
source: We considered the problem of inferring eight biophysical parameters in a HH single-compartment model, describing voltage-dependent sodium and potassium conductances and other intrinsic membrane properties, including neural noise, making the model stochastic by nature (Figure 4a, left).
evidence: This describes a property of the HH model used.

claim: The authors simulated the neuron's voltage response to the injection of a square wave of depolarizing current for the HH model.
source: We simulated the neuron's voltage response to the injection of a square wave of depolarizing current, and defined the model output 𝐱 used for inference as the number of evoked action potentials along with six additional features of the voltage response (Figure 4a, right, details in Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the simulation protocol.

claim: The model output used for inference was defined as the number of evoked action potentials along with six additional features of the voltage response for the HH model.
source: We simulated the neuron's voltage response to the injection of a square wave of depolarizing current, and defined the model output 𝐱 used for inference as the number of evoked action potentials along with six additional features of the voltage response (Figure 4a, right, details in Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the features used for inference.

claim: The variance of the posterior was narrower for some parameters than for others in the HH model, indicating that the seven data features constrain some parameters strongly but others only weakly.
source: The variance of the posterior was narrower for some parameters than for others, indicating that the seven data features constrain some parameters strongly (such as the potassium conductance), but others only weakly (such as the adaptation time constant).
evidence: This is a result from the HH model inference.

claim: Genetic algorithms are commonly used to fit parameters of deterministic biophysical models.
source: Genetic algorithms are commonly used to fit parameters of deterministic biophysical models (Druckmann et al., 2007; Hay et al., 2011; Van Geit et al., 2016; Gouwens et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes a common approach with citations.

claim: Genetic algorithms can return multiple data-compatible parameters, but they do not perform inference and their outputs depend strongly on user-defined goodness-of-fit criteria.
source: While genetic algorithms can also return multiple data-compatible parameters, they do not perform inference (i.e. find the posterior distribution), and their outputs depend strongly on user-defined goodness-of-fit criteria.
evidence: This describes limitations of genetic algorithms.

claim: The parameter-settings favored by IBEA produced simulations whose summary features were as similar to the observed data as those obtained by SNPE high-probability samples.
source: When comparing a state-of-the-art genetic algorithm (Indicator Based Evolutionary Algorithm, IBEA, [Bleuler et al., 2003; Zitzler and Künzli, 2004; Van Geit et al., 2016]) to SNPE, we found that the parameter-settings favored by IBEA produced simulations whose summary features were as similar to the observed data as those obtained by SNPE high-probability samples (Appendix 1—figure 10).
evidence: This is a result comparing SNPE to IBEA with citations.

claim: High-scoring IBEA parameters were concentrated in small regions of the posterior, that is, IBEA did not identify the full space of data-compatible models.
source: However, high-scoring IBEA parameters were concentrated in small regions of the posterior, that is, IBEA did not identify the full space of data-compatible models.
evidence: This is a result comparing SNPE to IBEA.

claim: Posterior simulations matched the observed data only in those features that had been used for inference in the HH model.
source: Posterior simulations matched the observed data only in those features that had been used for inference (e.g. applying SNPE to spike counts alone identified parameters that generated the correct number of spikes, but for which spike timing and subthreshold voltage time course were off, Figure 4e).
evidence: This is a result from the feature comparison.

claim: For some parameters in the HH model, providing more data features brought the peak of the posterior closer to the ground truth and also decreased uncertainty.
source: For some parameters, such as the potassium conductance, providing more data features brought the peak of the posterior (the posterior mode) closer to the ground truth and also decreased uncertainty.
evidence: This is a result from the feature comparison.

claim: SNPE can be used to study the effect of additional data features in reducing parameter uncertainty.
source: While SNPE can be used to study the effect of additional data features in reducing parameter uncertainty, this would not be the case for methods that only return a single best-guess estimate of parameters.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the feature comparison.

claim: SNPE can reveal how information from multiple data features imposes collective constraints on channel and membrane properties in the HH model.
source: These results show that SNPE can reveal how information from multiple data features imposes collective constraints on channel and membrane properties in the HH model.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the HH model results.

claim: The authors inferred HH parameters for eight in vitro recordings from the Allen Cell Types database.
source: We also inferred HH parameters for eight in vitro recordings from the Allen Cell Types database using the same current-clamp stimulation protocol as in our model (Allen Institute for Brain Science, 2016; Teeter et al., 2018; Figure 4f, Appendix 1—figure 9).
evidence: This describes an application to real data with citations.

claim: Simulations based on the SNPE-inferred posterior closely resembled the original data for each of the eight Allen Cell Types recordings.
source: In each case, simulations based on the SNPE-inferred posterior closely resembled the original data (Figure 4f).
evidence: This is a result from the Allen Cell Types data.

claim: While inferred parameters differed across recordings, some parameters were consistently more strongly constrained than others for the Allen Cell Types data.
source: We note that while inferred parameters differed across recordings, some parameters (the spike threshold, the density of sodium channels, the membrane reversal potential and the density of potassium channels) were consistently more strongly constrained than others (the intrinsic neural noise, the adaptation time constant, the density of slow voltage-dependent channels and the leak conductance) (Appendix 1—figure 9).
evidence: This is a result from the Allen Cell Types data.

claim: The electrophysiological responses measured by the current-clamp protocol can be approximated by a single-compartment HH model.
source: Overall, these results suggest that the electrophysiological responses measured by this current-clamp protocol can be approximated by a single-compartment HH model, and that SNPE can identify the admissible parameters.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the Allen Cell Types results.

claim: SNPE can identify the admissible parameters for the single-compartment HH model given Allen Cell Types data.
source: Overall, these results suggest that the electrophysiological responses measured by this current-clamp protocol can be approximated by a single-compartment HH model, and that SNPE can identify the admissible parameters.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the Allen Cell Types results.

claim: The authors aimed to demonstrate how the full posterior distribution obtained with SNPE can lead to novel scientific insights using the pyloric network of the stomatogastric ganglion (STG).
source: We next aimed to demonstrate how the full posterior distribution obtained with SNPE can lead to novel scientific insights. To do so, we used the pyloric network of the stomatogastric ganglion (STG) of the crab Cancer borealis, a well-characterized neural circuit producing rhythmic activity.
evidence: This describes the motivation for the STG application.

claim: In the STG circuit, similar network activity can arise from vastly different sets of membrane and synaptic conductances.
source: In this circuit, similar network activity can arise from vastly different sets of membrane and synaptic conductances (Prinz et al., 2004).
evidence: This describes a known property of the STG with citation.

claim: The authors investigated whether data-consistent sets of membrane and synaptic conductances are connected in parameter space for the STG.
source: We first investigated whether data-consistent sets of membrane and synaptic conductances are connected in parameter space, as has been demonstrated for single neurons (Taylor et al., 2006), and, second, which compensation mechanisms between parameters of this circuit allow the neural system to maintain its activity despite parameter variations.
evidence: This describes a research question with citation.

claim: The authors investigated which compensation mechanisms between parameters of the STG circuit allow the neural system to maintain its activity despite parameter variations.
source: We first investigated whether data-consistent sets of membrane and synaptic conductances are connected in parameter space, as has been demonstrated for single neurons (Taylor et al., 2006), and, second, which compensation mechanisms between parameters of this circuit allow the neural system to maintain its activity despite parameter variations.
evidence: This describes a research question.

claim: Answering the questions about the STG requires characterizing higher dimensional parameter spaces than those accessed previously.
source: While this model has been studied extensively, answering these questions requires characterizing higher dimensional parameter spaces than those accessed previously.
evidence: This explains why SNPE is needed for the STG.

claim: SNPE can be used to identify the posterior distribution over both membrane and synaptic conductances of the STG (31 parameters total).
source: We demonstrate how SNPE can be used to identify the posterior distribution over both membrane and synaptic conductances of the STG (31 parameters total) and how the full posterior distribution can be used to study the above questions at the circuit level.
evidence: This describes a capability of SNPE for the STG.

claim: The full posterior distribution can be used to study questions about connectivity and compensation mechanisms at the circuit level for the STG.
source: We demonstrate how SNPE can be used to identify the posterior distribution over both membrane and synaptic conductances of the STG (31 parameters total) and how the full posterior distribution can be used to study the above questions at the circuit level.
evidence: This describes a capability enabled by SNPE.

claim: For some biological systems, multiple parameter sets give rise to the same system behavior.
source: For some biological systems, multiple parameter sets give rise to the same system behavior (Prinz et al., 2004; Marder and Goaillard, 2006; Gutierrez et al., 2013; Fisher et al., 2013; Marder et al., 2015; Alonso and Marder, 2019).
evidence: This describes a known property of biological systems with citations.

claim: Neural systems can be robust to specific perturbations of parameters, yet highly sensitive to others, properties referred to as sloppiness and stiffness.
source: In particular, neural systems can be robust to specific perturbations of parameters (O'Leary et al., 2014; Marder et al., 2015; O'Leary and Marder, 2016), yet highly sensitive to others, properties referred to as sloppiness and stiffness (Goldman et al., 2001; Gutenkunst et al., 2007; Machta et al., 2013; O'Leary et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes properties of neural systems with citations.

claim: The authors studied how perturbations affect model output using a model and data of the pyloric rhythm in the crustacean stomatogastric ganglion (STG).
source: We studied how perturbations affect model output using a model (Prinz et al., 2004) and data (Haddad and Marder, 2018) of the pyloric rhythm in the crustacean stomatogastric ganglion (STG).
evidence: This describes the model and data used with citations.

claim: The STG model describes a triphasic motor pattern generated by a well-characterized circuit.
source: This model describes a triphasic motor pattern generated by a well-characterized circuit (Figure 5a).
evidence: This describes the STG model.

claim: The STG circuit consists of two electrically coupled pacemaker neurons (anterior burster and pyloric dilator, AB/PD), modeled as a single neuron, as well as two types of follower neurons (lateral pyloric (LP) and pyloric (PY)), all connected through inhibitory synapses.
source: The circuit consists of two electrically coupled pacemaker neurons (anterior burster and pyloric dilator, AB/PD), modeled as a single neuron, as well as two types of follower neurons (lateral pyloric (LP) and pyloric (PY)), all connected through inhibitory synapses (details in Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the STG circuit.

claim: Eight membrane conductances are included for each modeled neuron in the STG, along with seven synaptic conductances, for a total of 31 parameters.
source: Eight membrane conductances are included for each modeled neuron, along with seven synaptic conductances, for a total of 31 parameters.
evidence: This describes the parameters of the STG model.

claim: The STG model has been used to demonstrate that virtually indistinguishable activity can arise from vastly different membrane and synaptic conductances.
source: This model has been used to demonstrate that virtually indistinguishable activity can arise from vastly different membrane and synaptic conductances in the STG (Prinz et al., 2004; Alonso and Marder, 2019).
evidence: This describes prior work on the STG model with citations.

claim: The authors extended the STG model to include intrinsic neural noise on each neuron.
source: Here, we build on these studies and extend the model to include intrinsic neural noise on each neuron (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes a modification to the STG model.

claim: The authors applied SNPE to infer the posterior over 24 membrane parameters and 7 synaptic parameters (31 parameters in total) for the STG.
source: We applied SNPE to infer the posterior over 24 membrane parameters and 7 synaptic parameters, that is, 31 parameters in total.
evidence: This describes the application of SNPE to the STG.

claim: The authors applied SNPE to an extracellular recording from the STG of the crab Cancer borealis which exhibited pyloric activity.
source: We applied SNPE to an extracellular recording from the STG of the crab Cancer borealis (Haddad and Marder, 2018) which exhibited pyloric activity (Figure 5b), and inferred the posterior distribution over all 31 parameters based on 18 salient features of the voltage traces, including cycle period, phase delays, phase gaps, and burst durations (features in Figure 5B, posterior in Figure 5c, posterior over all parameters in Appendix 1—figure 11, details in Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the application of SNPE to STG data with citation.

claim: The posterior distribution for the STG has high probability over extended value ranges for many membrane and synaptic conductances.
source: Consistent with previous reports, the posterior distribution has high probability over extended value ranges for many membrane and synaptic conductances.
evidence: This is a result from the STG inference.

claim: Two samples from the STG posterior with widely disparate parameters from each other both exhibit activity highly similar to the experimental observation.
source: To verify that parameter settings across these extended ranges are indeed capable of generating the experimentally observed network activity, we sampled two sets of membrane and synaptic conductances from the posterior distribution. These two samples have widely disparate parameters from each other (Figure 5c, purple dots, details in Materials and methods), but both exhibit activity highly similar to the experimental observation (Figure 5d, top left and top right).
evidence: This is a result from the STG inference.

claim: The authors investigated the geometry of the parameter space producing pyloric rhythms in the STG.
source: We then investigated the geometry of the parameter space producing these rhythms (Achard and De Schutter, 2006; Alonso and Marder, 2019).
evidence: This describes an analysis of the STG results with citations.

claim: The authors wanted to identify directions of sloppiness in the STG parameter space.
source: First, we wanted to identify directions of sloppiness, and we were interested in whether parameter settings producing pyloric rhythms form a single connected region, as has been shown for single neurons (Taylor et al., 2006), or whether they lie on separate 'islands'.
evidence: This describes a research question with citation.

claim: The authors algorithmically identified a path through parameter space along which pyloric activity was maintained.
source: Starting from the two parameter settings showing similar activity above, we examined whether they were connected by searching for a path through parameter space along which pyloric activity was maintained. To do this, we algorithmically identified a path lying only in regions of high posterior probability (Figure 5c, white, details in Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes an analysis of the STG results.

claim: Along the high-probability path in the STG parameter space, network output was tightly preserved, despite a substantial variation of the parameters.
source: Along the path, network output was tightly preserved, despite a substantial variation of the parameters (voltage trace 1 in Figure 5d, Appendix 1—figure 12).
evidence: This is a result from the STG analysis.

claim: The authors inspected directions of stiffness by perturbing parameters off the high-probability path in the STG parameter space.
source: Second, we inspected directions of stiffness by perturbing parameters off the path. We applied perturbations that yield maximal drops in posterior probability (see Materials and methods for details), and found that the network quickly produced non-pyloric activity (voltage trace 2, Figure 5d; Goldman et al., 2001).
evidence: This describes an analysis of the STG results with citation.

claim: When perturbing parameters off the high-probability path in the STG parameter space, the network quickly produced non-pyloric activity.
source: Second, we inspected directions of stiffness by perturbing parameters off the path. We applied perturbations that yield maximal drops in posterior probability (see Materials and methods for details), and found that the network quickly produced non-pyloric activity (voltage trace 2, Figure 5d; Goldman et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a result from the STG analysis with citation.

claim: In identifying paths and perturbations in the STG parameter space, the authors exploited the fact that SNPE provides a differentiable estimate of the posterior.
source: In identifying these paths and perturbations, we exploited the fact that SNPE provides a differentiable estimate of the posterior, as opposed to parameter search methods which provide only discrete samples.
evidence: This describes an advantage of SNPE for the STG analysis.

claim: The pyloric network can be robust to specific perturbations in parameter space, but sensitive to others.
source: Overall, these results show that the pyloric network can be robust to specific perturbations in parameter space, but sensitive to others, and that one can interpolate between disparate solutions while preserving network activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the STG analysis.

claim: One can interpolate between disparate solutions while preserving network activity in the STG.
source: Overall, these results show that the pyloric network can be robust to specific perturbations in parameter space, but sensitive to others, and that one can interpolate between disparate solutions while preserving network activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the STG analysis.

claim: The STG analysis demonstrates the flexibility of SNPE in capturing complex posterior distributions.
source: This analysis demonstrates the flexibility of SNPE in capturing complex posterior distributions, and shows how the differentiable posterior can be used to study directions of sloppiness and stiffness.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the STG analysis.

claim: The differentiable posterior from SNPE can be used to study directions of sloppiness and stiffness.
source: This analysis demonstrates the flexibility of SNPE in capturing complex posterior distributions, and shows how the differentiable posterior can be used to study directions of sloppiness and stiffness.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the STG analysis.

claim: Experimental and computational studies have shown that stable neural activity can be maintained despite variable circuit parameters.
source: Experimental and computational studies have shown that stable neural activity can be maintained despite variable circuit parameters (Prinz et al., 2004; Marder and Taylor, 2011; O'Leary, 2018).
evidence: This describes prior work with citations.

claim: Stable neural activity despite variable circuit parameters can emerge from two sources: either the variation of a certain parameter barely influences network activity at all, or variations of several parameters influence network activity, but their effects compensate for one another.
source: This behavior can emerge from two sources (Marder and Taylor, 2011): either, the variation of a certain parameter barely influences network activity at all, or alternatively, variations of several parameters influence network activity, but their effects compensate for one another.
evidence: This describes possible mechanisms with citation.

claim: The authors investigated compensation mechanisms by using the posterior distribution over membrane and synaptic conductances of the STG.
source: Here, we investigated these possibilities by using the posterior distribution over membrane and synaptic conductances of the STG.
evidence: This describes an analysis of the STG.

claim: Many parameters in the STG seem only weakly constrained and only weakly correlated when inspecting pairwise marginals.
source: We began by drawing samples from the posterior and inspecting their pairwise histograms (i.e. the pairwise marginals, Figure 6a, posterior over all parameters in Appendix 1—figure 11). Consistent with previously reported results (Taylor et al., 2009), many parameters seem only weakly constrained and only weakly correlated (Figure 6b).
evidence: This is a result from the STG analysis with citation.

claim: Pairwise marginals are averages over many network configurations, where all other parameters may take on diverse values, which could disguise that each individual configuration is finely tuned.
source: However, this observation does not imply that the parameters of the network do not have to be finely tuned: pairwise marginals are averages over many network configurations, where all other parameters may take on diverse values, which could disguise that each individual configuration is finely tuned.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the pairwise marginals.

claim: When parameters were sampled independently from their posterior histograms, the resulting circuit configurations rarely produced pyloric activity, indicating that parameters have to be tuned relative to each other.
source: Indeed, when we sampled parameters independently from their posterior histograms, the resulting circuit configurations rarely produced pyloric activity, indicating that parameters have to be tuned relative to each other (Appendix 1—figure 14).
evidence: This is a result from the STG analysis.

claim: The approach of independently setting parameters can be problematic: although each parameter individually is in a realistic range, the network as a whole is not.
